title: Capacity Scaling QuarterScope: Strategy, OKR Mapping & Operational Milestones for Dedicated Autoscale
creator: Maya Patel
description: QuarterScope doc to translate strategic OKRs into a sequenced, measurable roadmap for Dedicated Capacity autoscale. The objective is to define milestones, success metrics, and operational runbooks necessary to reduce tail latency during surges, lower per-token cost through smarter warm-pools and reservoir policies, and provide predictable burst capacity for enterprise customers. This plan covers cross-functional deliverables across Product, Engineering (serving runtime + autoscale controller), Customer Reliability, and Solutions. It emphasizes a two-track approach: (1) Capacity economics and policy: pre-warming, reservation hedges, surge corridors; (2) Control plane and observability: autoscale APIs, guardrails, and cost-attribution dashboards.
acceptance_criteria:
- OKR mapping completed and approved by GTM and Eng leads
- Milestone plan published with owners and dates
- Two canary experiments defined (warm-pool sizing & fastpath fallback) with success thresholds
- Observability signals defined and dashboards scoped (latency p50/p95, cost per 1k tokens, queue times)
- Runbook and rollback criteria drafted for production autoscale launches
decisions: Adopt dual-reservoir model (steady vs surge) for pool allocation; avoids single-pool exhaustion
Default autoscale policy will prioritize latency-SLO tiers; cost-optimized fallback uses quantized model variants
Expose per-customer burst budget as a simple API field (burst_budget_minutes) rather than custom SLAs for MVP
milestones: Milestone 1 (by 2025-03-15): OKR alignment doc + stakeholder signoff
Milestone 2 (by 2025-03-31): Autoscale policy spec and API contract (ENG owner assigned)
Milestone 3 (by 2025-04-18): Observatory dashboards and alerting for capacity signals
Milestone 4 (by 2025-04-30): Canary experiment A (pre-warm sizing) executed and analyzed
Milestone 5 (by 2025-05-12): Canary experiment B (fastpath fallback) executed; go/no-go recommendation
tasks: PM: Draft OKRs and map to engineering milestones; share with execs
Eng: Implement autoscale API endpoints and policy engine hooks (ENG-28934)
Eng: Add capacity attribution labels to token billing pipeline for per-route cost visibility
Reliability: Draft runbook for surge events and define rollback criteria
Data: Build experiment metrics queries for p50/p95 latency, queue depth, and cost per 10k tokens
GTM: Prepare customer messaging templates for early access partners and user docs
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Pre-warm pools increase cost if not tightly coupled to demand forecasts; Mitigation: pilot with 3 customers and use conservative sizing; auto-shrink after 10 minutes of inactivity
Risk: Autoscale oscillation causing instability; Mitigation: introduce cooldown windows, smoothing and hysteresis in controller
Risk: Incorrect cost attribution leading to billing disputes; Mitigation: instrument per-customer telemetry and expose interim cost dashboards during pilot
success_metrics: Reduce tail latency (p95) during bursts by 30% for P1 customers
Lower average cost-per-1k-tokens for burst traffic by 12% vs baseline via reservoir warm-pools
Achieve predictable time-to-serve 95% of burst requests within configured latency SLO for dedicated pools
Pilot adoption: 3 enterprise customers onboarded to early access and provide feedback
communication_plan: Weekly sync with Eng leads (Wed 10:30am PT) to review progress
Bi-weekly stakeholder digest email with milestone updates and key signals
#prod-capacity Slack channel for real-time experiment telemetry and post-mortems
